rule: IF pdhC (K00627) absent AND ctaA (K02259) present AND coxL (K03520) present THEN has uses_O2
grounding_reasons: pdhC: a pathway gene required absent - the rule covers organisms without it (another enzyme or a lineage), not the pathway itself; ctaA: part of the pathway; coxL present: aerobic-lifestyle signal consistent with the rule
conditions: pdhC absent: no pyruvate dehydrogenase E2 (on its own this says little about oxygen — most organisms lack it) | ctaA present: heme A synthase: makes heme a for aa3 oxidase | coxL present: aerobic CO dehydrogenase large subunit
logic: The rule requires the pathway itself (ctaA). It requires pdhC to be absent, so it covers only the organisms that run this physiology without pdhC — one branch of it, not all. Its lifestyle markers (coxL → aerobic) agree with the aerobic lifestyle the trait requires, so the rule reads the pathway and the conditions it runs under together.
